So the pattern is "Some A are not B, therefore some B are not A". This swaps the subject and predicate of an O-proposition, which is not a valid inference in general.

**Checking each option against this pattern.**

- B: "Some people are not selfish" means some P are not S. The conclusion "People are not all selfish" means some P are not S. The subject is not swapped, so this is an equivalent restatement and a different form.
- C: "A good motive does not necessarily have a good effect" means some good motives lack good effects. The conclusion is "some good results do not come from good motives". This is the same swap pattern.
- D: "Some southerners are not Cantonese" means some S are not C. The conclusion is "some C are not S". This is the same swap pattern.
